summary: The model (training AUC 0.9605 on 242 patients) is a linear score plus three gated corrections, passed through a sigmoid. The direct terms carry most of the signal (switching them to their mean drops training AUC to 0.8402): vessels coloured, a flat ST slope, blood pressure, male sex and cholesterol add risk. The oldpeak gate adds risk with ST depression, opening at almost no depression when the thallium scan is abnormal (99 of 107 such patients have it on) but rarely with a normal scan (11 of 135). A blood-pressure gate, open for 156 of the 160 patients without exercise angina, cancels the blood-pressure term for them: in the typical case their risk is 26% at 120 mm Hg and 24% at 180 mm Hg, against 21% and 81% with exercise angina. An age brake for patients with normal fasting sugar makes predicted risk fall with age from about 60 years (typical case with a reversible defect), and pushes risk down for fixed-defect patients (fitted to 15 rows). The annotated model reproduces the network to 3.3e-16.

resisted: No part resisted.
